[Examples](similar-problems.qmd) · **Authoring guide** · [Workflow](similar-problems-workflow.qmd)

Start with a working `math-exercise`, enable generation, and describe what a useful
variation should change. Shared YAML supplies the course guidance; a one-line
exercise directive supplies the exception. No separate quiz configuration is needed.

## Enable it explicitly

Similar problems is **off by default**. Enable it in `_quarto.yml` for a course,
or in the front matter of one page:

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  similar: true
  policy-files: feedback/similar-problems.yml
  policy: {default: similar-practice}
  generation-policy: {default: similar-practice}
```

This is the configuration used on the [examples page](similar-problems.qmd).
`policy` selects teaching feedback; `generation-policy` selects generation
instructions. Here the same dictionary serves both purposes. They may also select
different names. Loading a policy file alone neither selects it nor enables
generation. An omitted `generation-policy` uses the shipped generation baseline;
it does not automatically select the teaching policy.

Use `#| similar: true` to enable one exercise, or `#| similar: false` to switch
one off even when the course enables it. The exam profile and builds without AI
keep generation off. Copy-prompt mode cannot generate a checked practice problem;
the learner must use Direct API.

## Define course guidance once

Create `feedback/similar-problems.yml`, relative to the project root:

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  policies:
    similar-practice:
      base-prompt: >-
        Use the notation and methods in the original exercise. Keep problems
        self-contained and nontrivial. Use exact rational or integer givens.
        For vector problems keep the coordinate count at most five; change
        the number of vectors or their dependencies to change difficulty.
      harder: Increase the reasoning required by one natural step.
      easier: Reduce the number of steps or provide more guidance.
      same: Give a fresh problem requiring the same method and effort.
```

Policies use the same flat dictionary, parser and inheritance rules for teaching
and generation. A policy may contain hint `steps` as well as direction guidance.
Generation ignores the hint steps and does not advance the hint counter;
teaching feedback ignores `harder`, `easier` and `same`.

The `{default: ...}` selection adds common instructions while retaining the
shipped integration baseline. A scalar selection, such as
`generation-policy: similar-practice`, replaces its integration base instructions.
Use the map form above when you want to retain the shipped starting prompt.

`policy-files` accumulate from project to page, while the nearest policy selector
wins. Named policies may use `extends`; omitted fields inherit and supplied strings
replace inherited strings. Exercise-ID overrides and explicit exercise selections
apply afterward. See the [full policy reference](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-libs/blob/main/docs/feedback-policies.md)
for the complete rules.

## Refine a single exercise

````markdown
```{math-exercise}
#| label: derivative-practice
#| vars: x
#| harder: Introduce a product or chain rule, with small integer coefficients.
#| simpler: Use a single power function.
#| same: Change the power and coefficient; keep the power rule sufficient.
Differentiate $f(x)=x^2$. $f'(x)=$ _[2*x].
```
````

The existing `#|` directive syntax is used throughout. In a policy the direction is
`easier`; in an exercise `#| simpler:` supplies that direction's addon. Only the
chosen direction's addon is appended to the resolved policy. These directives
do not enable generation by themselves.

Select a different generation policy on one exercise with
`#| generation-policy: another-policy`; use `#| feedback-policy:` for its teaching
policy. Keep exercise labels stable so that overrides and saved work keep their
intended identity.

## Choose a response and enforce important constraints

| Response | Authoring approach |
|---|---|
| Symbolic expression | Start with ordinary `_[answer]` fields and the intended grading mode. |
| Fixed vector or matrix | Use `vec[...]` or `mat[...;...]`. Generated matrix answers use the same fixed grid widget. |
| A mathematical property | Reuse a trusted authored checker, as in the independence example. The model receives a compact contract, never permission to write checker code. |

Generated practice follows the original grading rules, including form restrictions,
precision/tolerance and partial credit. A new problem should exercise the same
mathematical skill rather than escape those rules.

Prompt guidance helps steer generation; it is not an enforced mathematical bound.
For an important restriction, supply a checker that rejects violations. The
[independence example](similar-problems.qmd#linear-independence-with-an-authored-check)
limits vectors to five coordinates in both the prompt and the trusted checker.
Its admitted matrix `A` can vary, while its checker code remains fixed. Arbitrary
new checker programs, JSXGraph responses and resizable matrices are outside phase 1.

Computed answers are preferred. Where no supported recipe fits, an independent
solve is required and the expected answer remains labelled unverified. Even a
computed answer can match an inappropriate recipe: authors should test whether
the resulting questions are clear, worthwhile and within the intended syllabus.

## Review before sharing

Try all three directions and several repetitions. Check the question, its expected
answer, input widget and feedback, including a deliberately wrong answer. Reload
to confirm saved work, and test the local report flow. Verify that an exercise
with `#| similar: false` stays off.

Students generate their own practice at runtime. A Quarto build does not call an
LLM or pre-generate the questions. Your colleagues need a configured provider to
try generation; the ordinary authored questions can be checked without one.
